newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore says attacks on soldiers isolated and few.
newsitem.headline: Singapore says attacks on soldiers isolated and few.

text.p: Singapore said on Wednesday that two attacks on its soldiers in the north Australian state of Queensland were isolated and that authorities there were taking measures to prevent further assaults.
"The incidents involving SAF (Singapore Armed Forces) soldiers are isolated and few," a Defence Ministry spokesman told Reuters.
"We are in touch with the Rockhampton authorities and they are taking measures to prevent such further incidents," the spokesman said.

Rockhampton city police chief superintendent Wayne King said earlier on Wednesday police were investigating one incident of assault in which a soldier got a blow to the head and another of assault and robbery.
"We're only investigating two matters that have been reported to us and one of them certainly has no racial overtones and the second one, who knows?" he said.
An Australian newspaper said the two officers robbed were subjected to racial abuse, and that two Singaporean Air Force women received anti-Asian taunts and were pelted with eggs.
It quoted a Queensland town mayor, Barbara Wildin, as saying there had been five attacks she said stemmed from the anti-Asian immigration furore sparked by independent MP Pauline Hanson.

"I think these incidents come from this nonsense put up by Pauline Hanson," Wildin said, referring to Hanson's anti-Asian immigration campaign that has triggered a row in Australia and drawn criticism of Canberra from some Asian newspapers.

But the Rockhampton police's King said: "We're not aware of any racial overtones in relation to the Singapore soldiers that are here. Really I think it's just a thing that has been blown all out of proportion by some comments that have been made."
About 1,000 members of the SAF are in Australia for an exercise in the Australian Defence Forces' training area near Rockhampton on the central Queensland coast.
Australian Defence Minister Ian McLachlan said reports of racially motivated attacks against Singapore soldiers were exaggerated.
"But whatever the cause, we regard any instance like this as an abomination and extremely regrettable," he told parliament.
